items.definition: Slightly ill or not feeling well, but not seriously sick.
examples: I'm feeling a bit under the weather, so I'll skip the party tonight.
She looked under the weather after the long flight.
My brother lives abroad, so we only meet once in a blue moon.
He cooks once in a blue moon, usually when he has guests.

items.definition: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed when they meet for the first time.
examples: The trainer began with a quick quiz to break the ice.
A joke about the weather is often enough to break the ice.

items.headword: hit the nail on the head
items.definition: To describe a situation or a problem in exactly the right way.
examples: You hit the nail on the head when you said the team lacks leadership.
Her short comment hit the nail on the head.

items.definition: The final problem in a series of annoying events, after which you cannot accept the situation any longer.
examples: When the train was cancelled again, that was the last straw and I bought a car.
Losing my keys was the last straw after such a terrible morning.

items.definition: To decide to do something unpleasant or difficult that you have been avoiding.
examples: I finally bit the bullet and booked an appointment with the dentist.
The company will have to bite the bullet and cut some jobs.

items.definition: Back at the very beginning, because earlier efforts have failed and you must start again.
examples: The deal collapsed, so we're back to square one.
After the software crashed, I was back to square one with my essay.

items.definition: To stop working, or stop an activity, for the rest of the day.
examples: We've been decorating since nine, so let's call it a day.
It's nearly six; shall we call it a day?

items.definition: To tell someone a secret by mistake or too early.
examples: Don't spill the beans about the surprise party!
Someone spilled the beans, and now everyone knows about the wedding.

items.definition: Something that seems bad at first but later turns out to be good.
examples: Missing that flight was a blessing in disguise, as it crashed into a storm later.
Losing the job turned out to be a blessing in disguise; she started her own business.
collocations: turn out to be a blessing in disguise

items.definition: Not something you particularly like or enjoy.
examples: Horror films are not really my cup of tea.
Camping is more my sister's cup of tea than mine.

items.definition: To learn how to do something, especially something that was confusing at first.
examples: It took me a week to get the hang of the new software.
Once you get the hang of it, parking is easy.

items.definition: Quick to understand what is happening and to react well.
examples: Our new assistant is really on the ball; she spotted the error at once.
You need to be on the ball in this job because things change quickly.

items.definition: A lot of fuss and excitement about something unimportant.
examples: The newspapers called it a scandal, but it was just a storm in a teacup.
The argument over the office kettle was a storm in a teacup.
